synopsis: Blender appears as a procedural scene-generation tool for construction, with a 2023 Automation in Construction example scripting scenes using real lighting captured on two dates; CropCraft, an open-source Blender and Python tool dated November 2025, extends its use to agricultural fields [f3733, f3789, f4133, f3787]. Blender pipelines are also listed among systems that automatically provide labels for procedural and simulated scenes, with both independent and vendor evidence attached to that claim [f3975, f3976]. For construction worker detection, a secondary summary in the 2025 Midjourney paper attributes a 50% reduction in required real images and a 16% detector-performance improvement to Kim et al.’s 2023 Blender-rendered synthetic-worker study [f7049, f7050]. In sensor simulation, SynFog (2024) paired a physical fog chamber with a one-to-one Blender virtual twin and found simulated per-channel trends consistently followed real captures as fog density increased, but this evidence is on-road [f4563]. The listed construction and excavation examples, including procedural Blender datasets, are camera-centric, so these facts do not establish equivalent coverage for other sensor modalities or heavy off-road automatic-braking validation [f4137, f4563].
